h-uruk-period.summary: Uruk grows into one of the first large cities. Its period gives its name to the age.

h-cuneiform.summary: Scribes in southern Mesopotamia turn accounting marks into cuneiform. It is the earliest known writing system.

h-ziggurat-of-ur.summary: King Ur-Nammu raises a stepped temple tower for the moon god at Ur.

h-akkadian-empire.summary: Sargon of Akkad unites the city-states of southern Mesopotamia. Many call it the first empire.

image.title: Royal Akkadian Head from Nineveh (inv.nr. IM 11331).jpg

h-gilgamesh.summary: Scribes join older Sumerian poems into one Akkadian epic. It is the oldest surviving narrative literature.

h-code-of-hammurabi.summary: Hammurabi of Babylon has a code of laws carved on a tall stone stele.

image.title: P1050763 Louvre code Hammurabi face rwk.JPG

h-battle-of-kadesh.summary: Ramesses II of Egypt meets the Hittite army of Muwatalli II on the Orontes River.

h-bronze-age-collapse.summary: Kingdoms across the eastern Mediterranean fall or shrink. Cities such as Ugarit are destroyed.

h-narmer.summary: Many scholars see Narmer as the first king of a unified Egypt. He founds the First Dynasty.

image.title: Narmer palette (obverse) (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Photo: This image has been extracted from another file

h-pyramid-of-djoser.summary: Egypt builds its first pyramid as a tomb for King Djoser.

h-great-pyramid.summary: Workers build the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu over about 26 years. It is the oldest of the Seven Wonders.

image.title: Great Pyramid of Giza - Pyramid of Khufu.jpg

h-kerma.summary: A Nubian kingdom grows at Kerma on the Nile. At its height it rivals Egypt.

h-hyksos.summary: Kings of foreign origin rule Lower and Middle Egypt from Avaris in the Nile Delta.

image.title: Painting of foreign delegation in the tomb of Khnumhotep II circa 1900 BCE (Detail mentioning "Abisha the Hyksos" in hieroglyphs).jpg

h-nok.summary: A farming culture in central Nigeria later makes the region's earliest known terracotta sculptures.

image.title: Kneeling figure, Nok culture, terracotta, Honolulu Museum of Art, 8348.1.JPG

h-bantu-expansion.summary: Bantu-speaking farmers begin a slow spread across central and southern Africa. It lasts for thousands of years.

h-amarna.summary: Akhenaten builds a new capital and puts the sun disc Aten above the other gods.

h-tutankhamun.summary: The boy king restores Egypt's traditional gods after Akhenaten. He dies at about 19.

h-newgrange.summary: Farmers in Ireland build a great passage tomb above the River Boyne. It is older than the pyramids.

h-otzi.summary: A man dies high in the Alps, and the ice preserves his body. It is Europe's oldest known natural mummy.

h-stonehenge.summary: People dig the first ditch and bank on Salisbury Plain. The stones are set up in later centuries.

h-knossos.summary: The Minoans of Crete build a palace at Knossos. It becomes their largest center.

image.title: Bull leaping fresco, Knossos, 1600-1450 BC, AMH, 258363.jpg

h-thera-eruption.summary: A huge volcanic eruption destroys Akrotiri on Thera. Its exact date is still debated.

h-mycenae.summary: The Mycenaean Greeks extend the great walls of their citadel at Mycenae.

image.title: Path upto the Lion Gate, Mycenae (28693130016).jpg

h-sintashta.summary: People of the southern Urals build fortified settlements. Many scholars link them to the earliest Indo-Iranian languages.

h-indus-valley.summary: Planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro flourish along the Indus. The civilisation covers more land than Egypt and Mesopotamia combined.

h-rigveda.summary: Poets in the northwest of India compose Sanskrit hymns. They become the oldest of the four Vedas.

h-liangzhu.summary: A jade-working society builds a large center near modern Hangzhou. It may be one of East Asia's first states.

image.title: British Museum Chinese jade Neolithic period Liangzhu culture Cong 11022019 1433.jpg

h-sannai-maruyama.summary: Jōmon people in northern Japan settle a village with hundreds of pit houses.

h-erlitou.summary: A Bronze Age society grows in the Yellow River valley. Many archaeologists see it as China's first state.

h-shang-dynasty.summary: Shang kings rule from capitals such as Yin. Their oracle bones hold the earliest known Chinese writing.

image.title: Inscribed oracle bone, Shang Dynasty, Xiaotun, Anyang, Henan.jpg

h-battle-of-muye.summary: King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king. The Zhou dynasty begins.

h-caral.summary: Communities on the coast of Peru build large plazas and mounds. It is the oldest known civilization in the Americas.

h-valdivia.summary: Villagers on the Ecuador coast make some of the earliest pottery in the Americas.

image.title: Valdivia Female Figurine 2600-1500 BCE Brooklyn Museum.jpg

h-poverty-point.summary: People in the lower Mississippi valley build great earthen ridges and mounds.

image.title: Mound A at the Monumental Earthworks Poverty Point World Heritage Site.jpg

h-paso-de-la-amada.summary: Villagers on the Pacific coast of Chiapas build a court for the Mesoamerican ballgame.

h-olmec-san-lorenzo.summary: The Olmec make San Lorenzo their main center. They carve colossal stone heads.

h-austronesian-expansion.summary: Seafarers from Taiwan begin settling the islands of Southeast Asia. Their descendants later reach the Pacific and Madagascar.

h-lapita.summary: Austronesian seafarers with stamped pottery settle Island Melanesia. They are ancestors of the Polynesians.

image.title: Decorated piece of Lapita pottery from the Bourewa site in Fiji.jpg

h-second-great-awakening.summary: Camp meetings and revivals sweep the American frontier. Rival churches compete for converts, as Joseph Smith later recalls.

image.title: Camp meeting of the Methodists in N. America J. Milbert del M. Dubourg sculp (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Dubourg, M., engraver Milbert, Jacques Gérard, 1766-1840 , artist

h-restoration-movement.summary: Preachers seek to restore New Testament Christianity without creeds. Sidney Rigdon led such a congregation before he was baptized in 1830.

image.title: Pioneers in the great religious reformation of the nineteenth century, eng. by J.C. Buttre.tif
image.artist: Engraving by J.C. Buttre; design by J.D.C. McFarland

h-lewis-and-clark.summary: An army party maps the Missouri River and crosses the Rockies. Their reports open the West to American settlers.

h-war-of-1812.summary: The United States fights Britain over trade and the frontier. British troops burn Washington in 1814.

image.title: War of 1812 Montage.jpg
image.artist: Clockwise, from top: George Munger, John David Kelly, Anton Otto Fischer, William Emmons, Edward Percy Moran

h-year-without-a-summer.summary: A volcanic eruption cools the world, and frost kills New England crops. The Smith family leaves Vermont for Palmyra, New York.

image.title: Joseph Mallord William Turner (1775-1851) - Chichester Canal - T03885 - Tate.jpg

h-shaka-zulu.summary: A young king remakes Zulu warfare and unites many peoples by force. The Zulu become the strongest power in southern Africa.

h-gran-colombia.summary: Simón Bolívar's congress joins Venezuela and New Granada in one republic. Spanish rule in South America is breaking.

h-missouri-compromise.summary: Congress admits Missouri as a slave state and Maine as a free one. Slavery in Missouri later fuels conflict with Latter-day Saints.

image.title: Charles Bird King, Henry Clay, 1821, NGA 195003 (cropped).jpg

h-greek-independence.summary: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule and win a kingdom of their own. Europe's powers intervene on their side.

h-cherokee-syllabary.summary: A Cherokee silversmith invents a writing system for his language. Within a few years most Cherokees can read it.

h-brazil-independence.summary: Prince Pedro breaks with Portugal and becomes Brazil's emperor.

image.title: Pedro Américo - Independência ou Morte - Google Art Project.jpg

h-monroe-doctrine.summary: President Monroe warns Europe against new colonies in the Americas.

image.title: Uncle Sam Straddles the Americas Cartoon.jpg

h-erie-canal.summary: A canal links the Hudson River to Lake Erie. It runs through Palmyra, where the Book of Mormon was printed.

image.title: Sunset over the Erie Canal in North Tonawanda, NY..jpg

h-andrew-jackson.summary: A frontier general becomes president and expands the power of the office. His term spans the Church's first years.

h-indian-removal-act.summary: Congress authorizes moving eastern tribes west of the Mississippi. The first missionaries to the Lamanites preach to Delaware removed to Kansas.

image.title: President Andrew Jackson's Message to Congress "On Indian Removal", 12-06-1830, Page 1-7 (6023478288).jpg

h-liverpool-manchester-railway.summary: Steam trains run between Liverpool and Manchester. Railways soon spread across Britain and the world.

h-finney-rochester.summary: A revival preacher stirs a city near Palmyra. Western New York becomes known as the burned-over district.

image.title: Charles g finney.jpg
image.artist: Photo: version of Christian History vol. VII, n. 4, issue 20

h-nat-turner.summary: Enslaved people in Virginia rise in revolt and are crushed. Southern states pass harsher slave laws.

image.title: Horrid massacre in Virginia LCCN98510363.tif
image.artist: Miscellaneous Items in High Demand, PPOC, Library of Congress

h-nullification-crisis.summary: South Carolina declares a federal tariff void, and Jackson threatens force. D&C 87, given that December, foresees war beginning there.

h-black-hawk-war.summary: Sauk leader Black Hawk returns to Illinois and is driven out by militia. The fighting opens the region to settlers.

image.title: George Catlin - Múk-a-tah-mish-o-káh-kaik, Black Hawk, Prominent Sac Chief - 1985.66.2 - Smithsonian American Art Museum.jpg

h-cholera-1832.summary: A worldwide cholera pandemic reaches Canada and the United States. It strikes Zion's Camp in Missouri in 1834.

h-slavery-abolition-act.summary: Parliament passes a law to free the enslaved across most of the British Empire.

image.title: Coat of Arms of the United Kingdom (1816-1837).svg

h-texas-revolution.summary: Settlers in Texas revolt and found a republic. The Alamo falls before the victory at San Jacinto.

h-great-trek.summary: Dutch-speaking settlers leave the Cape by wagon for the interior. Their trek parallels other mass migrations of the age.

h-oregon-trail.summary: Migrants begin crossing the plains by wagon. The pioneers later follow the same river valleys to the Salt Lake Valley.

image.title: Albert Bierstadt - Emigrants Crossing the Plains (1867).jpg

h-panic-of-1837.summary: Banks fail across the United States, and a long depression follows. The Kirtland Safety Society collapses in the same crisis.

h-queen-victoria.summary: An 18-year-old queen begins a reign of 63 years. The first Latter-day Saint missionaries reach England the same summer.

h-trail-of-tears.summary: Soldiers march the Cherokee to Indian Territory, and thousands die. The same year Latter-day Saints are driven from Missouri.

h-daguerreotype.summary: Louis Daguerre's process makes the first practical photographs. Portraits of Church leaders soon follow.

h-morse-telegraph.summary: The first long telegraph line opens between Washington and Baltimore. News now moves faster than any rider.

h-great-disappointment.summary: Followers of William Miller expect Christ's return on a set day. When it passes, the movement splinters.

h-irish-famine.summary: Potato blight brings mass starvation to Ireland. More than two million people emigrate.

h-mexican-american-war.summary: The United States invades Mexico and takes the Southwest. The Mormon Battalion marches to California in this war.

image.title: Nebel Mexican War 12 Scott in Mexico City (cropped).jpg

h-california-gold-rush.summary: Workers at Sutter's Mill find gold, and a rush begins. Former Mormon Battalion men are among the workers.

image.title: 1850 Woman and Men in California Gold Rush.jpg

h-revolutions-of-1848.summary: Uprisings spread across Europe, demanding constitutions and national rights. Most are put down within two years.

h-seneca-falls.summary: The first women's rights convention meets in western New York. Its declaration calls for women's right to vote.

h-mark-in-alexandria.summary: Church tradition says Mark, the Gospel writer, brought the faith to Egypt. The Coptic Church counts him as its founder.

image.title: Codexaureus 21.jpg
image.artist: Scriptorium of the Lorsch Abbey ( Hofschule Karls des Großen ), Germany

h-amanitore.summary: Amanitore and her son Natakamani build temples at Naqa and Meroë. Their reign is the best-recorded time of the kingdom.

image.title: Aegyptisches Museum Berlin InvNr7261 20080313 Barkenuntersatz Natakamani Amanitore aus Wad Ban Naga 1.jpg

h-periplus-erythraean-sea.summary: The Periplus lists ports from Egypt to India. It names Adulis, Aksum, and Rhapta on the East African coast.

image.title: WELLSTED(1838) p2.829 RUINS AT BERENICE.jpg
image.artist: Photo: This file is from the Mechanical Curator collection , a set of over 1 million images scanned from out-of-copyright books and released to Flickr Commons by the British Library in London, England. View image on Flickr View all images from book View catalogue entry for book .

h-kingdom-of-aksum.summary: Aksum grows into a trading power on the Red Sea. Its ships link Rome and India through the port of Adulis.

h-hero-of-alexandria.summary: Hero describes the aeolipile, a sphere spun by steam. He also writes on mirrors, pumps, and surveying.

h-ptolemy-almagest.summary: Ptolemy's Almagest sets out the Earth-centered sky. His Geography lists the known world with coordinates.

h-garamantes.summary: Desert farmers in the Fezzan dig tunnels to tap fossil water. Their capital, Garama, trades with Rome across the sand.

h-septimius-severus.summary: Septimius Severus, born in Leptis Magna, wins the throne. He builds up his home city with a new forum and basilica.

h-perpetua-and-felicity.summary: A young noblewoman and an enslaved woman are killed for their faith. Perpetua's prison diary survives.

image.title: Perpetua, Felicitas, Revocatus, Saturninus and Secundulus (Menologion of Basil II).jpg
image.artist: Authors of Menologion of Basil II (circa 985 AC, Constantinople), Byzantine manuscript illuminators : Pantoleon with Georgios, Michael the Younger, Michael of Blachernae, Symeon, Symeon of Blachernae, Menas, and Nestor ( Online on Vatican site )

h-anthony-the-great.summary: Anthony leaves his village to live alone in the wilderness. His example starts Christian monasticism.

h-aksumite-coins.summary: King Endubis strikes gold, silver, and bronze coins. Aksum is the only African state south of Egypt to do so.

h-pachomius.summary: Pachomius gathers monks under one rule and one roof. Communal monasteries spread from here across the Christian world.

h-augustine-of-hippo.summary: A Numidian convert becomes bishop of Hippo. His Confessions and City of God shape Western Christian thought.

image.title: Saint Augustine by Philippe de Champaigne.jpg

h-nag-hammadi.summary: Thirteen papyrus books of Gnostic and other early Christian texts are sealed in a jar. They include the Gospel of Thomas.

image.title: El Evangelio de Tomás-Gospel of Thomas- Codex II Manuscritos de Nag Hammadi-The Nag Hammadi manuscripts.png

h-serapeum-closed.summary: The great temple of Serapis is shut as the old religion is banned. It had housed the daughter library of Alexandria.

image.title: Alexandria - Pompey's Pillar - view of ruins.JPG

h-hypatia.summary: A mob kills the philosopher and mathematician Hypatia. She had taught astronomy and geometry in the city.

h-vandals-take-carthage.summary: Gaiseric's Vandals seize Rome's richest African province. Their fleet then raids across the Mediterranean.

image.title: Münze 50 Denari - Gelimer - König der Vandalen (cropped).jpg

h-lydenburg-heads.summary: Iron Age farmers in southern Africa shape seven terracotta heads. They are the oldest known sculptures south of the equator.

h-madagascar-settled.summary: Sailors from the Indonesian islands cross the Indian Ocean in outrigger canoes. Their language becomes Malagasy.

h-vandalic-war.summary: Belisarius lands near Carthage and ends the Vandal kingdom in a year. Africa is Roman again for a century.

h-nubia-christianity.summary: The kingdom of Nobatia on the Nile accepts the faith from Egypt. Nubian churches are painted for the next 900 years.

h-kairouan-founded.summary: Arab armies build a garrison town in what is now Tunisia. Its great mosque makes it a center of learning.

image.title: Great Mosque of Kairouan courtyard and portico.jpg

h-kanem-empire.summary: A kingdom grows on the caravan routes across the Sahara. It becomes one of the longest-lived states in Africa.

h-cairo-founded.summary: The Fatimids lay out a new capital north of Fustat. It soon holds al-Azhar, one of the oldest universities.

h-wang-mang.summary: A Han official founds the short Xin dynasty. He abolishes slavery and redistributes land, then falls to rebellion.

image.title: WUL-he21 01467 新鐫繪像東西漢全傳 01 (王莽).jpg

h-eastern-han.summary: Liu Xiu claims the throne and makes Luoyang his capital. By his death the Eastern Han rules all of China.

h-king-of-na-gold-seal.summary: Guangwu gives a gold seal to an envoy from the state of Na. It is Japan's first dated appearance in written history.

image.title: King of Na gold seal.jpg
image.artist: Original uploader: User:金翅大鹏鸟 at zh.wikipedia

h-white-horse-temple.summary: Emperor Ming founds the White Horse Temple for two monks from India. Tradition calls it China's first Buddhist temple.

h-ban-chao.summary: The Han general secures the Tarim Basin and the Silk Road. He sends Gan Ying west to find Rome.

h-zhang-heng-seismoscope.summary: A bronze vessel drops a ball to show the direction of a distant earthquake. Zhang also maps the stars.

h-yellow-turban-rebellion.summary: Peasants led by Daoist healers rise against the Han court. The war that follows breaks the dynasty's power.

image.title: Zhang Jue Qing portrait.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Taken from Gongjin's Campaign Memorials: a Three Kingdoms Wiki Zengxiang quantu Sanguoyanyi

h-three-kingdoms.summary: Wei, Shu, and Wu fight for the fallen Han empire. Their generals and strategists become China's best-loved legends.

image.title: Dai Jin-Looking Three Times at the Thatched Hut.jpg

h-himiko.summary: A shaman queen of Wa, early Japan, is named in Chinese records. Wei's emperor calls her a friend of Wei.

h-mogao-caves.summary: Monks cut cave shrines into a cliff on the Silk Road. Over a thousand years they fill with paintings and scrolls.

h-battle-of-fei-river.summary: A small Eastern Jin army routs the Former Qin invasion. North and south China stay divided for two more centuries.

image.title: Guo Xu - Portrait of Xie An (undated).jpg

h-gwanggaeto-stele.summary: King Jangsu of Goguryeo sets up a stone to honor his father. It is the chief written source for early Korea.

h-yungang-grottoes.summary: The Northern Wei court orders giant Buddhas cut into a sandstone cliff. Indian and Chinese styles meet in the carving.

h-longmen-grottoes.summary: The Northern Wei move to Luoyang and begin carving Buddhas by the Yi River. Work continues for 600 years.

h-buddhism-reaches-japan.summary: The king of Baekje sends a Buddha image and sutras to the Japanese court. The Soga clan takes up the new faith.

h-xuanzang.summary: A Chinese monk travels to India for Buddhist texts and studies at Nalanda. He returns with 657 books to translate.

h-alopen.summary: A Syriac missionary of the Church of the East reaches the Tang court. The Xi'an Stele of 781 records his welcome.

image.title: Nestorian-Stele-Budge-plate-III.jpg
image.artist: Stele text by Nestorian monk Jingjing . Photo either made by Henri Havret, or a local collaborator of his, or reproduced from an earlier Chinese source. There is a caption in Havret's 1895 publication, possibly explaining the provenance, but it's hardly legible.

h-taika-reform.summary: After the fall of the Soga clan, the court remakes Japan on the Chinese model. Land and taxes come under the emperor.

h-wu-zetian.summary: The only woman to rule China in her own name founds her Zhou dynasty. She favors Buddhism and the examination system.

image.title: 唐后行從圖 (局部) - 武則天.png
image.artist: Likely to be Zhang Xuan (张萱)

h-an-lushan-rebellion.summary: A frontier general marches on the Tang capitals. The eight-year war leaves the dynasty weakened for good.

h-heian-kyo.summary: Emperor Kanmu lays out a grid city on the model of Chang'an. It stays the imperial seat for a thousand years.

h-thomas-in-india.summary: Tradition says the apostle Thomas landed on the Kerala coast. The Saint Thomas Christians trace their church to him.

h-muziris-roman-trade.summary: Monsoon winds carry Roman ships to the Malabar coast each year. Pepper and gems go west, gold and wine come east.

h-gautamiputra-satakarni.summary: The greatest Satavahana king restores his dynasty's power in the Deccan. Its capital is Pratishthana on the Godavari.

h-kanishka.summary: Kanishka rules from Central Asia to the Ganges. He supports Buddhism, and his coins show gods of many faiths.

image.title: KanishkaCoin3.JPG
image.artist: No machine-readable author provided. World Imaging assumed (based on copyright claims).

h-rabatak-inscription.summary: A stone in Bactrian names Kanishka's ancestors and the gods who gave him kingship. It fixed the Kushan family tree.

image.title: Surkh Kotal inscription.jpg
image.artist: Photo: cropped of 3-dimensional elements as advised on Commons:When_to_use_the_PD-Art_tag. Non-creative 2-dimensional image of an ancient inscription (2nd century CE)

h-hephthalites.summary: The White Huns defeat the Kidarites and press on Persia and India. The Turks and Sasanians bring them down together.

image.title: Hephthalite wearing the crown of Peroz I Late 5th century CE.jpg

h-alchon-huns-india.summary: Toramana's Alchon Huns push into central India. The invasions help bring down the Gupta Empire.

h-sigiriya.summary: A Sri Lankan king makes a fortress on a 180-meter column of granite. Its painted maidens still look out from the cliff.

h-aryabhata.summary: At 23 he sets out arithmetic, algebra, and astronomy in verse. He holds that the Earth turns on its axis.

h-mahabodhi-temple.summary: A brick tower rises where the Buddha is said to have gained enlightenment. It is the holiest Buddhist pilgrimage site.

h-badami-caves.summary: Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist shrines are carved into a sandstone cliff at the Chalukya capital.

image.title: Vishnu image inside cave number 3 in Badami.jpg

h-harsha.summary: Harsha unites the north from Kannauj and hosts the pilgrim Xuanzang. His empire breaks up at his death.

h-shore-temple.summary: The Pallavas build a granite temple on the beach of their port. It is among the oldest stone temples in south India.

h-kailasa-temple.summary: Rashtrakuta masons cut a whole temple downward out of one cliff. It is the largest rock-cut temple in the world.

image.title: Kailash temple (Ellora cave no 15) at Verul.png

h-pala-empire.summary: The chiefs of Gauda elect Gopala as king. His Buddhist dynasty builds great monasteries and trades with Southeast Asia.

image.title: WLA haa Standing Buddha Pala dynasty.jpg

h-rajaraja-i.summary: The Chola king conquers the south and northern Sri Lanka. His navy reaches the Maldives.

image.title: Raraja detail.png
image.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Venu62~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

h-buddhas-of-bamiyan.summary: Two giant Buddhas are cut into a cliff on the road between India and China. The Taliban destroyed them in 2001.

h-songtsen-gampo.summary: The king unites the Tibetan plateau and moves his court to Lhasa. He brings in Buddhism and a script.

h-afrasiab-murals.summary: A Sogdian house is painted with envoys from China, Korea, and Persia. It shows the Silk Road at its busiest.

image.title: Afrasiab - details from The Ambassadors' Painting 3 - great procession.JPG

h-samanid-empire.summary: A Persian dynasty governs Khorasan and Transoxiana. Persian poetry and learning revive at its court.

h-trung-sisters.summary: Two sisters lead the Vietnamese against the Chinese governor and rule for three years. They are national heroines.

h-funan.summary: A trading state grows in the Mekong Delta. Roman, Indian, and Chinese goods are found at its port, Óc Eo.

h-champa-founded.summary: A local official throws off Han rule on the coast of central Vietnam. The Cham kingdoms last until 1832.

image.title: Ganesh, My Son E5, 7th century, Quang Nam - Museum of Cham Sculpture - Danang, Vietnam - DSC01715.JPG

h-sri-ksetra.summary: The Pyu wall a city on the Irrawaddy larger than any before Angkor. Buddhist texts are stamped on gold leaves.

h-chenla.summary: Khmer rulers from the interior take over Funan's lands. Their temples at Sambor Prei Kuk come before Angkor.

h-dvaravati.summary: Mon towns in the Chao Phraya basin adopt Buddhism and Indian script. Their stone Wheels of the Law survive.

h-pagan-fortified.summary: King Pyinbya fortifies a small town that grows into the first Burmese empire. Thousands of temples later fill its plain.

image.title: Old Bagan, Myanmar, Ancient Buddhist temple in Bagan plains.jpg

h-prambanan.summary: A Hindu king consecrates a temple to Shiva near Buddhist Borobudur. It is the largest Hindu temple in Indonesia.

h-laguna-copperplate.summary: A debt is cancelled in writing on a copper plate. It is the oldest known document from the Philippines.

image.title: Laguna Copperplate Inscription in the National Museum of Anthropology.jpg

h-teutoburg-forest.summary: Arminius ambushes Varus in the Teutoburg Forest. Rome gives up its plans to hold Germany east of the Rhine.

h-roman-conquest-of-britain.summary: Claudius sends four legions across the Channel. Within fifty years most of England and Wales is a Roman province.

image.title: Bust of Emperor Claudius - Altes Museum, Berlin (52671298090).jpg

h-boudica.summary: The queen of the Iceni burns Colchester, London, and St Albans. Rome crushes the rising within a year.

h-pliny-natural-history.summary: Pliny the Elder's encyclopedia gathers what Romans knew of nature, geography, and art. It mentions the Essenes by the Dead Sea.

image.title: First page from the Editio Princeps of the Pliny's "Historia Naturalis".jpg

h-colosseum.summary: Vespasian begins the amphitheater with spoils from Judea, and Titus opens it. It seats some 50,000 people.

h-pantheon-rome.summary: A concrete dome 43 meters wide is raised over the temple of all the gods. It is still the largest unreinforced dome.

h-hadrians-wall.summary: A stone wall with forts runs 117 kilometers across northern Britain. It marks the empire's edge.

h-galen-in-rome.summary: The physician from Pergamon becomes doctor to emperors. His books rule Western medicine for 1,400 years.

h-antonine-plague.summary: Soldiers returning from the East bring a deadly epidemic, likely smallpox. It kills millions across the empire.

h-crisis-of-the-third-century.summary: Fifty years of civil war, plague, and invasion nearly break the empire. Diocletian's reforms end the chaos.

h-wulfila-gothic-bible.summary: Wulfila makes an alphabet for the Goths and translates the scriptures. It is the oldest long text in a Germanic language.

image.title: Germania, 1882 1020017 (4358323359) (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Fondo Antiguo de la Biblioteca de la Universidad de Sevilla from Sevilla, España

h-battle-of-adrianople.summary: Gothic refugees settled inside the empire destroy the eastern army and kill the emperor Valens.

image.title: Solidus of Valens (364–378) MET sf67-265-22s1.jpg
image.artist: Photo: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art . See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

h-edict-of-thessalonica.summary: Theodosius I orders all subjects to hold the Nicene faith. Other creeds are declared heresies.

h-jerome-vulgate.summary: Pope Damasus asks Jerome to revise the Latin Gospels. Jerome goes on to translate the Old Testament from Hebrew in Bethlehem.

h-sack-of-rome-410.summary: Alaric's Goths loot the city for three days. Rome had not fallen to an enemy in 800 years.

h-saint-patrick.summary: A Briton once enslaved in Ireland returns as a missionary bishop. His own Confession tells the story.

image.title: Our Lady's Island Church of the Assumption East Aisle Window Saint Patrick 2010 09 26.jpg

h-attila.summary: From the Hungarian plain Attila extorts gold from both Roman empires. He invades Gaul and Italy before his death.

image.title: Attila Hunnorum Rex Flagellum Dei Aquilejae Eversor Utini Instaurator.jpg

h-clovis.summary: A Frankish king conquers most of Gaul and accepts Catholic baptism. His Merovingian line rules for 250 years.

h-corpus-juris-civilis.summary: Jurists gather centuries of law into the Code, the Digest, and the Institutes. European civil law descends from it.

h-plague-of-justinian.summary: Bubonic plague arrives from Egypt and kills a fifth of Constantinople. It returns in waves for two centuries.

h-lombards-invade-italy.summary: A Germanic people crosses the Alps and takes most of the peninsula from the Byzantines. Lombardy keeps their name.

h-sutton-hoo.summary: An East Anglian king is buried in a ship with a helmet, gold, and silver. It was found intact in 1939.

h-gregory-the-great.summary: A former prefect of Rome reforms the Church and feeds the city. He sends missionaries to the English.

image.title: Gregory the Great with the Holy Spirit.jpg

h-augustine-of-canterbury.summary: Monks sent by Pope Gregory baptize King Æthelberht. Canterbury becomes the seat of the English church.

h-muslim-conquest-of-iberia.summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses from Africa and the Visigothic kingdom falls. Al-Andalus lasts for nearly 800 years.

h-byzantine-iconoclasm.summary: Emperors ban and destroy religious images. The dispute splits the Church for a century and strains ties with Rome.

h-bede.summary: A monk in Northumbria writes the Ecclesiastical History of the English People. He dates events from the birth of Christ.

h-battle-of-tours.summary: The Franks turn back an Umayyad army from al-Andalus. Charles's grandson will be Charlemagne.

h-great-mosque-of-cordoba.summary: Abd al-Rahman I builds a hall of striped arches on the site of a church. It is now the city's cathedral.

image.title: Mezquita de Córdoba desde el aire (Córdoba, España).jpg

h-book-of-kells.summary: Monks of Columba's order paint the four Gospels in Latin. Its pages are the finest of Celtic art.

h-iceland-settled.summary: Farmers from Norway claim an empty island in the North Atlantic. Their descendants write the sagas.

image.title: The Norwegians land in Iceland year 872.jpg

h-cyril-and-methodius.summary: Two brothers from Thessalonica devise the first Slavic alphabet. They translate the scriptures and liturgy.

image.title: Sv Kiril Metodij Zahari Zograf Trojanski mon 1848.jpg
image.artist: painted by Zahari Zograf (Захарий Христович Димитров)

h-bulgaria-christianized.summary: Boris I and his court are baptized by a mission from Constantinople. Bulgaria soon adopts the Slavic liturgy.

h-alfred-the-great.summary: Alfred holds off the Vikings and fortifies his towns. He translates Latin books into English.

image.title: Alfred the Great, silver penny; struck 875–880 (obverse).png

h-kievan-rus.summary: A Varangian prince makes Kiev the seat of the Rus'. The state he founds reaches from the Baltic to the Black Sea.

h-otto-the-great.summary: The German king is crowned in Rome, reviving the imperial title in the West. It becomes the Holy Roman Empire.

h-vladimir-baptism.summary: The prince of Kiev accepts Orthodox Christianity and marries a Byzantine princess. His people follow him into the Dnieper.

h-mishnah.summary: Judah the Prince gathers the oral law into six orders. It becomes the core of the Talmud.

h-mani.summary: A prophet from Babylonia presents his faith to Shapur I. Manichaeism spreads from Africa to China.

image.title: Seal of Mani (cleaned up). Seal with figure of Mani, possibly 3rd century CE, possibly Irak. Cabinet des Médailles, Paris.jpg

h-dura-europos-synagogue.summary: A synagogue on the Euphrates is painted with scenes from the Hebrew Bible. A Roman rampart preserved the walls.

h-battle-of-edessa.summary: The Sasanian king defeats Valerian and takes him prisoner. Rock reliefs in Persia show the emperor kneeling.

h-zenobia.summary: The queen of a desert trading city takes Egypt and Syria. Aurelian defeats her and leads her through Rome in chains.

h-armenia-christian.summary: King Tiridates III is converted by Gregory the Illuminator. Armenia is the first state to make Christianity official.

h-diocletianic-persecution.summary: Diocletian orders churches razed and scriptures burned. It is Rome's last and harshest persecution.

image.title: Istanbul Archaeology Museum Bust of Diocletian, from Nikomedia, Izmit, end 3rd century AD 1536.jpg

h-church-of-the-holy-sepulchre.summary: A church rises over the sites held to be Golgotha and the tomb of Jesus. Pilgrims have come ever since.

image.title: Church of the Holy Sepulchre by Gerd Eichmann (cropped).jpg

h-codex-sinaiticus.summary: Scribes copy the whole Greek Bible onto parchment. It is the oldest complete New Testament.

h-council-of-ephesus.summary: Bishops condemn Nestorius and name Mary Theotokos, the bearer of God. The Church of the East goes its own way.

h-council-of-chalcedon.summary: Over 500 bishops define Christ as one person in two natures. The churches of Egypt, Syria, and Armenia reject it.

h-babylonian-talmud.summary: The academies of Sura and Pumbedita finish their commentary on the Mishnah. It becomes the central text of Judaism.

image.title: Talmud-Druck von Daniel Bomberg und Ambrosius Froben.jpg

h-saint-catherines-monastery.summary: Justinian walls a monastery around the traditional burning bush. It is the oldest monastery still in use.

h-sasanian-jerusalem-614.summary: Khosrow II's army captures the city during the long war with Byzantium. Heraclius later wins it back.

image.title: Capital of Khosrow II, Taq-e Bostan.jpg

h-battle-of-the-yarmuk.summary: Arab armies destroy the Byzantine field army in six days. Syria and Palestine pass to the caliphate.

h-battle-of-nahavand.summary: The last Persian army is broken. Yazdegerd III flees east and the caliphate takes Iran.

h-umayyad-caliphate.summary: Mu'awiya makes the caliphate hereditary. In ninety years it reaches from Spain to the Indus.

image.title: The Umayyad Mosque, the Courtyard, Damascus, Syria.jpg

h-battle-of-karbala.summary: The grandson of Muhammad dies with his small band against the Umayyad army. Shia Muslims mourn the day each year.

image.title: Brooklyn Museum - Battle of Karbala - Abbas Al-Musavi - cropped.jpg

h-abbasid-revolution.summary: A revolt from Khurasan overthrows the Umayyads. The new dynasty soon builds Baghdad and rules for 500 years.

h-al-khwarizmi.summary: A scholar at the House of Wisdom sets out methods for solving equations. The words algebra and algorithm come from his work.

image.title: Madrid - Ciudad Universitaria, Monumento a Muhammad al-Juarismi (cropped).jpg

h-great-mosque-of-samarra.summary: The caliph al-Mutawakkil builds the largest mosque in the world. Its spiral minaret still stands.

h-aleppo-codex.summary: Masoretic scribes finish the most accurate copy of the Hebrew Bible. Maimonides later endorsed it.

image.title: Aleppo Codex Joshua 1 1.jpg
image.artist: see en:Aleppo Codex ; scanned by http://www.aleppocodex.org

h-cahuachi.summary: Forty adobe mounds rise above the Nazca Lines. Pilgrims gather here from across the valley.

h-san-agustin.summary: Hundreds of carved guardians watch over tombs in the Colombian highlands. It is the largest necropolis in the Americas.

image.title: Parque Arqueológico de San Agustín-Mesita A 06.jpg

h-pachacamac.summary: A shrine to the creator god grows on the coast south of Lima. Pilgrims come to its oracle for 1,300 years.

h-quimbaya-classic.summary: Craftsmen in the Cauca valley cast gold and copper figures and flasks. Their work is the finest in ancient Colombia.

image.title: Cacique Quimbaya de oro (M. América, Madrid) 01.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Photograph: Luis García ( Zaqarbal ), 6 April 2008.

h-tierradentro.summary: Underground chambers reached by spiral stairs are painted in red, black, and white. They hold the bones of the dead.

h-wari-empire.summary: From Ayacucho the Wari rule much of Peru with roads and provincial centers. The Inca later follow their model.

image.title: Jar, Huari Empire, Peru, 600-900 AD, ceramic - Fowler Museum - University of California, Los Angeles - DSC02374.jpg

h-marajoara.summary: People at the mouth of the Amazon build mounds and paint elaborate pottery. They farm the floodplain.

image.title: Burian urn, AD 1000-1250, Marajoara culture - AMNH - DSC06177 b.jpg

h-ashurbanipal-library.summary: The Assyrian king collects clay tablets on every subject. More than 30,000 tablets and fragments survive.

h-fall-of-nineveh.summary: An alliance of Babylonians and Medes sacks the Assyrian capital. The Assyrian Empire soon collapses.

h-achaemenid-empire.summary: Cyrus of Persia founds the Achaemenid Empire. Its kings come to rule from Egypt to the Indus.

h-persepolis.summary: Persian kings begin a great ceremonial capital. Alexander's army burns its palaces in 330 BCE.

h-alexander-invades-persia.summary: Alexander of Macedon crosses into Asia and conquers the Persian Empire. He dies at Babylon in 323 BCE.

image.title: Alexander Mosaic detail of Alexander the Great (3x4 cropped).jpg
image.artist: Photo: This image has been extracted from another file

h-seleucid-empire.summary: One of Alexander's generals takes the eastern part of his empire. His dynasty rules from Mesopotamia to Syria.

image.title: 201209071746a Berlin Pergamonmuseum, Tetradrachme Seleukos' I, Silber, Pergamon, 281-280 v.u.Z.jpg

h-parthian-empire.summary: The Arsacid dynasty founds an Iranian empire. It later becomes Rome's great rival in the east.

image.title: Coin of Mithridates II of Parthia (obverse and reverse), Ray mint.jpg

h-olympic-games.summary: Greek tradition dates the first games at Olympia to this year.

h-founding-of-rome.summary: Roman tradition sets the city's founding in this year. Archaeology shows earlier villages on its hills.

h-athenian-democracy.summary: Cleisthenes gives power to an assembly of citizens. Athenian democracy grows from these reforms.

h-battle-of-marathon.summary: Athenian soldiers defeat the first Persian invasion of Greece.

image.title: Scene of the Battle of Marathon.jpg

h-parthenon.summary: Athens builds a temple to Athena on the Acropolis. It thanks the goddess for victory over Persia.

h-la-tene.summary: A Celtic Iron Age culture spreads across much of Europe. It lasts until the Roman conquest.

h-hannibal-alps.summary: The Carthaginian general leads his army and elephants over the Alps into Italy.

image.title: Carthago - 213-210 BC - silver shekel - head of Melqart - elefant - London BM TC-p74-42-Pan.jpg

h-caesar-assassinated.summary: Senators kill the Roman dictator during a Senate session. Civil war follows.

image.title: Vincenzo Camuccini - La morte di Cesare (cropped 3-2).jpg

h-augustus.summary: Octavian takes the name Augustus and rules as emperor. The Roman Republic gives way to the Empire.

h-scythians.summary: Mounted Scythian nomads become the dominant power on the western Eurasian steppe.

h-carthage.summary: Merchants from Tyre found Carthage in North Africa. It grows into a great sea power.

h-kushite-pharaohs.summary: Kings from Kush in Nubia rule Egypt as its Twenty-fifth Dynasty for nearly a century.

h-meroe.summary: The Kingdom of Kush rules from Meroë on the Nile for centuries.

h-library-of-alexandria.summary: Scholars gather at the great library of Ptolemaic Egypt. They study Homer, mathematics, and the stars.

h-djenne-djenno.summary: People settle a site in the inland Niger delta. It becomes one of West Africa's oldest towns.

image.title: Djenné Moschee.jpg
image.artist: The original uploader was Euronaut at German Wikipedia . Later versions were uploaded by Zahnstein at de.wikipedia .

h-the-buddha.summary: A wandering teacher in the Ganges plain founds Buddhism. Scholars debate the exact years of his life.

image.title: Buddha in Sarnath Museum (Dhammajak Mutra).jpg
image.artist: พระมหาเทวประภาส วชิรญาณเมธี (ผู้ถ่าย-ปล่อยสัญญาอนุญาตภาพให้นำไปใช้ได้เพื่อการศึกษาโดยอยู่ภา่ยใต้ cc-by-sa-3.0) ผู้สร้างสรรค์ผลงาน/ส่งข้อมูลเก็บในคลังข้อมูลเสรีวิกิมีเดียคอมมอนส์ - เทวประภาส มากคล้าย

h-maurya-empire.summary: Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire across northern India. It is one of the largest in Indian history.

h-edicts-of-ashoka.summary: The Maurya emperor Ashoka has moral teachings carved on pillars and rocks across India.

h-eastern-zhou.summary: The Eastern Zhou period begins. Local lords gain power as royal power weakens.

image.title: Bianzhong of Marquis Yi of Zeng.jpg

h-confucius.summary: The philosopher Kong Qiu teaches ethics and good government. His ideas shape China for millennia.

image.title: Confucius, fresco from a Western Han tomb of Dongping County, Shandong province, China (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Anonymous Chinese painter of the Western Han period

h-qin-unification.summary: The state of Qin conquers its rivals. Its king becomes the first emperor of China.

h-terracotta-army.summary: Thousands of clay soldiers are buried with the first emperor to guard him after death.

h-han-dynasty.summary: Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty after the fall of Qin. Han rule lasts about four centuries.

h-xiongnu.summary: Nomads of the eastern steppe unite under one leader. They become a great rival of Han China.

h-silk-road.summary: A Han envoy's journeys to Central Asia open trade routes to the west.

h-yayoi.summary: Rice farming and metalwork spread across the Japanese islands. Some scholars date the start earlier.

image.title: 東京国立博物館展示 銅鐸.JPG

h-la-venta.summary: After San Lorenzo declines, La Venta becomes the main Olmec city. Its people carve colossal heads.

h-chavin.summary: A religious center in the Peruvian Andes draws pilgrims from a wide region.

h-paracas.summary: An Andean society in southern Peru weaves some of the finest ancient textiles.

h-el-mirador.summary: The Maya build huge temples at El Mirador in the Petén. It peaks from the 3rd century BCE.

h-monte-alban.summary: The Zapotec build a hilltop city in the Oaxaca valley. It becomes their capital.

h-adena.summary: Woodland peoples in the Ohio valley build burial mounds and earthworks.

h-tonga-settled.summary: Seafarers of the Lapita culture reach Tonga. It is the first island settled in Polynesia.

image.title: Display of objects of the Lapita culture, Otago Museum, 2016-01-29.jpg

h-siege-of-jerusalem-70.summary: Roman legions take Jerusalem during the First Jewish Revolt. The temple is destroyed and never rebuilt.

image.title: (Venice) La distruzione del tempio di Gerusalemme -Francesco Hayez - gallerie Accademia Venice.jpg

h-sasanian-empire.summary: Ardashir defeats the last Parthian king. His Sasanian dynasty rules Iran until 651.

h-council-of-nicaea.summary: Bishops from across the Roman Empire meet at Nicaea. They issue the first form of the Nicene Creed.

h-hijrah.summary: Muhammad leaves Mecca for Medina. The year becomes the start of the Islamic calendar.

image.title: New York Public Library, Spencer Collection Turk. MS. 3 Siyar-i Nabî fol. 286r Jibril delivers to Muhammad a message from God telling him to leave Makka for Madina.jpg

h-dome-of-the-rock.summary: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik builds a shrine over the rock on the Temple Mount.

h-round-city-baghdad.summary: Caliph al-Mansur builds a round city on the Tigris. It becomes the Abbasid capital.

h-vesuvius-79.summary: Mount Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash.

h-trajan.summary: By the death of Emperor Trajan, Roman rule stretches farther than ever before.

h-edict-of-milan.summary: Constantine and Licinius agree to tolerate Christians across the Roman Empire.

h-constantinople.summary: Constantine makes the old city of Byzantium his new capital. It stays a capital for 1,100 years.

h-fall-of-western-rome.summary: Odoacer removes Romulus Augustulus. Many historians date the end of the Western Roman Empire here.

h-hagia-sophia.summary: The emperor Justinian completes a great domed church. It becomes the largest interior space in the world.

h-lindisfarne.summary: Norse raiders sack the abbey on Lindisfarne. Many date the start of the Viking Age here.

h-charlemagne.summary: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king as emperor in Rome.

image.title: Charlemagne denier Mayence 812 814.jpg
image.artist: Charlemagne. Autorité émettrice de monnaie indéterminé. Atelier monétaire. Émetteur

h-aksum-christianity.summary: Under King Ezana the Ethiopian kingdom of Aksum makes Christianity its state religion.

h-arab-conquest-egypt.summary: The Rashidun Caliphate takes Egypt from the Eastern Roman Empire.

h-igbo-ukwu.summary: Igbo-Ukwu becomes the capital of the Kingdom of Nri. Its artisans cast detailed bronzes.

image.title: Bronze ornamental staff head, 9th century, Igbo-Ukwu.JPG

h-ghana-empire.summary: The scholar al-Khwārizmī first names the West African empire of Ghana. It grows rich on Saharan trade.

h-kushan-empire.summary: The Yuezhi found an empire linking Central Asia and northern India along the Silk Road.

image.title: Coin of Kanishka depicting Gautam Buddha.jpg

h-gupta-empire.summary: The Guptas rule much of northern India. Science, art, and literature flourish.

image.title: Buddha in Sarnath Museum (Dhammajak Mutra).jpg
image.artist: พระมหาเทวประภาส วชิรญาณเมธี (ผู้ถ่าย-ปล่อยสัญญาอนุญาตภาพให้นำไปใช้ได้เพื่อการศึกษาโดยอยู่ภา่ยใต้ cc-by-sa-3.0) ผู้สร้างสรรค์ผลงาน/ส่งข้อมูลเก็บในคลังข้อมูลเสรีวิกิมีเดียคอมมอนส์ - เทวประภาส มากคล้าย

h-nalanda.summary: A Gupta emperor founds a great Buddhist center of learning. It draws students from across Asia.

h-ajanta.summary: Monks and patrons carve and paint Buddhist caves in western India. Older accounts date this phase earlier.

image.title: Ajanta (63).jpg
image.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Soman assumed (based on copyright claims).

h-chola-rise.summary: The Chola dynasty of southern India begins its imperial age.

image.title: Thanjavur temple.jpg
image.artist: The original uploader was Venu62 at English Wikipedia .

h-cai-lun-paper.summary: A Han court official makes paper from bark, hemp, rags, and fishnets. Paper soon replaces bamboo slips.

image.title: Cai-lun.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Tsien Tsuen-Hsuin (1985) Needham, Joseph, ed. Science and Civilisation in China: Volume 5, Chemistry and Chemical Technology, Part 1, Paper and Printing , Taipei : Caves Books, pp. 108–109 ISBN : 978-0-521-08690-5 . Etnografiska museet, Stockholm: 1935.50.3366.30

h-sui-dynasty.summary: The short Sui dynasty unites China after centuries of division.

h-tang-dynasty.summary: The Tang dynasty rules China for nearly three centuries. Trade and the arts flourish.

h-silla-unification.summary: Allied with Tang China, the kingdom of Silla conquers its rivals Paekche and Goguryeo.

h-nara.summary: Japan builds its first permanent imperial capital at Heijō-kyō, now Nara.

h-diamond-sutra.summary: A woodblock copy of a Buddhist text is printed in Tang China. It is often called the oldest surviving printed book.

image.title: Jingangjing.jpg
image.artist: The colophon, at the inner end, reads: Reverently [caused to be] made for universal free distribution by Wang Jie on behalf of his two parents on the 13th of the 4th moon of the 9th year of Xiantong [i.e. 11th May, CE 868 ].

h-srivijaya.summary: A Chinese monk studies at Srivijaya on Sumatra. The kingdom is a center of Buddhism and sea trade.

h-borobudur.summary: Builders in central Java raise a vast Buddhist monument in stone terraces.

h-khmer-empire.summary: Jayavarman II declares himself universal king. The Khmer Empire grows to rule much of mainland Southeast Asia.

h-gokturks.summary: The Göktürks overthrow the Rouran and found a steppe empire across Central Asia.

h-battle-of-talas.summary: Abbasid and Tibetan forces defeat a Tang army in Central Asia.

h-teotihuacan.summary: A planned city with great pyramids grows in the Valley of Mexico. At its height it is the largest in the Americas.

image.title: ZA77 Teotihuacán edo de mex Herberto de la rosa.jpg

h-moche.summary: The Moche build adobe pyramids and make fine pottery on Peru's north coast.

image.title: Moche - Portrait Vessel - Walters 482827 - Three Quarter.jpg

h-tiwanaku.summary: A highland city near Lake Titicaca leads the southern Andes.

h-pakal.summary: The Maya king Kʼinich Janaabʼ Pakal rebuilds Palenque. His tomb lies in the Temple of the Inscriptions.

h-maya-collapse.summary: Tikal, Palenque, Copán, and Calakmul decline and are abandoned. The causes are still debated.

h-chaco-canyon.summary: Ancestral Puebloans build great houses of stone in the American Southwest.

image.title: Chaco Culture NHP (8023723138).jpg
image.artist: Greg Willis from Denver, CO, usa

h-great-schism.summary: The Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches break communion. Scholars debate whether 1054 is the true turning point.

h-norman-conquest.summary: William of Normandy defeats Harold Godwinson at Hastings and takes the English crown.

h-university-of-bologna.summary: Students in Bologna organize to hire teachers of law. It grows into Europe's oldest university.

image.title: Seal of the University of Bologna.svg

h-magna-carta.summary: Rebel barons force the English king to accept limits on royal power.

image.title: Magna Carta (British Library Cotton MS Augustus II.106).jpg
image.artist: Original authors were the barons and King John of England . Uploaded by Earthsound .

h-hundred-years-war.summary: England and France fight a long series of wars over the French throne.

image.title: Schlacht von Azincourt.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Antoine Leduc, Sylvie Leluc et Olivier Renaudeau (dir.), D'Azincourt à Marignan. Chevaliers et bombardes, 1415-1515 , Paris, Gallimard / Musée de l'armée, 2015, p. 18-19, ISBN 978-2-07-014949-0

h-black-death.summary: A plague pandemic sweeps across Europe and kills a large part of its people.

h-gutenberg.summary: Johannes Gutenberg develops printing with movable metal type. His press later prints the Gutenberg Bible.

h-fall-of-constantinople.summary: The Ottoman army takes Constantinople after a 53-day siege. The Byzantine Empire ends.

image.title: Siege of Constantinople fresco, Moldovița monastery, Vatra Moldoviței, 2017.jpg

h-granada-1492.summary: The last Muslim kingdom in Iberia surrenders to Castile. Jews are expelled from Spain the same year.

h-first-crusade-jerusalem.summary: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem after a siege. The crusaders found the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

image.title: Taking of Jerusalem by the Crusaders, 15th July 1099.jpg

h-saladin-jerusalem.summary: The Ayyubid sultan Saladin takes Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin. The Third Crusade follows.

h-sack-of-baghdad.summary: Hulegu's Mongol army takes Baghdad and ends the Abbasid Caliphate there.

h-ain-jalut.summary: The Mamluks of Egypt defeat a Mongol army in Galilee. The Mongol advance west is halted.

image.title: Baybars, Medallion IV, Baptistère de Saint-Louis.jpg

h-ottoman-empire.summary: A Turkoman leader founds a small state in Anatolia. It grows into the Ottoman Empire.

h-tale-of-genji.summary: Murasaki Shikibu writes a long tale of the Japanese court. It is a classic of world literature.

h-bi-sheng.summary: A Song dynasty artisan prints with fired clay pieces, one for each character.

h-kamakura.summary: Warrior families rule Japan through a military government at Kamakura.

h-mongol-empire.summary: A council proclaims Temüjin ruler of all Mongols. His empire becomes the largest contiguous land empire.

image.title: YuanEmperorAlbumGenghisPortrait.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Digitized by National Palace Museum; file is directly from Shuge

h-yuan-dynasty.summary: The Mongol ruler Kublai Khan governs China as emperor of a new dynasty.

h-ming-dynasty.summary: The Ming drive out the Mongol Yuan rulers. Ming emperors rule China for nearly three centuries.

image.title: A Seated Portrait of Ming Emperor Taizu.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Oversize Scrolls of Painting and Calligraphy (2019 exhibit). Taipei: National Palace Museum. 巨幅書畫 (2019年展覽). 臺北: 國立故宮博物院.

h-zheng-he.summary: A Ming admiral leads seven great fleets across the Indian Ocean. They reach Arabia and East Africa.

h-forbidden-city.summary: The Ming build a vast palace complex in Beijing. It remains the imperial seat until 1924.

image.title: The Forbidden City - View from Coal Hill.jpg

h-timur.summary: The conqueror Timur rules Central Asia and Iran from Samarkand.

h-brihadisvara.summary: The Chola emperor Rajaraja I builds a towering temple to Shiva.

image.title: Brihadisvara Temple during Maha Shivaratri-WUS03611 (edit).jpg
image.artist: Original: Rainer Halama Derivative work: UnpetitproleX

h-delhi-sultanate.summary: Turkic rulers found a sultanate at Delhi. Its dynasties rule much of northern India for three centuries.

h-vijayanagara.summary: Two brothers found a south Indian empire with its capital at Vijayanagara, now Hampi.

h-angkor-wat.summary: The Khmer king Suryavarman II builds a vast temple at his capital.

h-majapahit.summary: Raden Wijaya founds a Javanese empire after a Mongol invasion. It comes to rule much of the archipelago.

h-ayutthaya.summary: A Thai kingdom rises at Ayutthaya. It lasts for more than four centuries.

h-great-zimbabwe.summary: Shona builders raise great stone walls in southern Africa. The city becomes a royal capital.

image.title: Conical Tower - Great Enclosure III (33736918448).jpg
image.artist: Andrew Moore from Johannesburg, South Africa

h-lalibela.summary: Churches are carved down into solid rock in the Ethiopian highlands. Tradition credits King Lalibela.

h-mansa-musa.summary: The ruler of Mali travels to Mecca with a vast entourage and much gold. Mali is at its height.

image.title: Catalan Atlas BNF Sheet 6 Mansa Musa (cropped).jpg

h-kilwa.summary: A Swahili trading city on the East African coast builds a great palace.

image.title: Flag used in the east coast of Tanzania according to a Portuguese 1576 map.svg

h-kongo.summary: A marriage alliance joins two peoples into the Kingdom of Kongo in central Africa.

image.title: Flag of the Kingdom of Kongo according to Giovanni Cavazzi da Montecuccolo.svg

h-songhai.summary: Sonni Ali of Songhai takes the great trading cities of the Niger.

h-lanse-aux-meadows.summary: Norse voyagers build a small settlement in North America. It is the only undisputed Norse site there.

image.title: Authentic Viking recreation.jpg
image.artist: Dylan Kereluk from White Rock, Canada

h-cahokia.summary: The Mississippian city by the Mississippi River has about 120 earthworks at its peak.

h-inca-rise.summary: The Inca state grows from the highlands around Cusco. It later becomes the largest empire in the Americas.

h-tenochtitlan.summary: The Mexica build their city on an island in Lake Texcoco. It becomes the Aztec capital.

h-chan-chan.summary: The Chimú rule the north coast of Peru from a vast adobe city. The Inca conquer them around 1470.

h-columbus-1492.summary: Christopher Columbus lands in the Bahamas for Spain. Lasting contact between Europe and the Americas begins.

h-hawaii-settled.summary: Polynesian voyagers reach the Hawaiian Islands and settle them.

image.title: Canoe hokulea under sail profile.jpg
image.artist: The original uploader was Mms7 at English Wikipedia .

h-rapa-nui-settled.summary: Voyagers reach one of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth. Its people later carve the moai statues.

h-aotearoa-settled.summary: East Polynesian voyagers settle New Zealand. Their descendants become the Māori.

image.title: 1863 Meeting of Settlers and Maoris at Hawke's Bay, New Zealand - Right.png

h-ninety-five-theses.summary: Martin Luther challenges the sale of indulgences. The Protestant Reformation grows from the dispute.

h-magellan-expedition.summary: A Spanish fleet sails west under Magellan. After his death, Elcano brings one ship home around the world.

image.title: Detail from a map of Ortelius - Magellan's ship Victoria.png

h-copernicus.summary: Nicolaus Copernicus places the Sun, not the Earth, at the center of the universe.

h-spanish-armada.summary: A great Spanish fleet sails to invade England and fails.

image.title: Launch of fireships against the Spanish Armada, 7 August 1588 RMG BHC0263.jpg

h-king-james-bible.summary: The Church of England publishes a new English translation of the Bible. It is read widely for centuries.

h-thirty-years-war.summary: Religious and political conflict tears through Central Europe. It is one of Europe's most destructive wars.

image.title: Carl Friedrich Lessing - The Siege (Defense of a Church Courtyard During the Thirty Years’ War) - Google Art Project.jpg

h-galileo-dialogue.summary: Galileo defends a Sun-centered universe in print. The Inquisition later puts him on trial.

h-peace-of-westphalia.summary: Two treaties end the Thirty Years' War. They shape the European system of states.

h-battle-of-vienna.summary: A relief army breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna. Ottoman expansion into Europe begins to reverse.

h-newton-principia.summary: Isaac Newton sets out his laws of motion and universal gravitation.

image.title: Newton's Principia title page.png
image.artist: The original uploader was Zhaladshar at English Wikisource .

h-saint-petersburg.summary: The tsar builds a new city on the Baltic. It becomes the capital of the Russian Empire.

h-storming-of-the-bastille.summary: Crowds in Paris seize a royal fortress. It becomes the symbol of the French Revolution.

h-safavid-iran.summary: The Safavids found a new Iranian empire and make Shia Islam its state religion.

image.title: Safavid Flag.svg
image.artist: Safavid_Flag.png : Orange Tuesday ( talk ) The original uploader was Orange Tuesday at English Wikipedia . derivative work: Himasaram ( talk )

h-suleiman.summary: The Ottoman Empire reaches its height under Suleiman. His armies besiege Vienna in 1529.

h-atlantic-slave-trade.summary: European traders ship about 12.75 million Africans to the Americas as slaves. Up to 2 million die on the voyage.

h-tondibi.summary: A Moroccan army with firearms defeats the Songhai Empire near Gao.

h-nzinga.summary: Nzinga leads the Ambundu kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba against Portuguese conquest.

h-gondar.summary: Emperor Fasilides settles his court at Gondar and builds a stone castle.

h-cape-colony.summary: The Dutch East India Company builds a supply post at the Cape of Good Hope. A colony grows from it.

image.title: Flag of the Dutch East India Company.svg

h-asante-empire.summary: Osei Tutu unites the Asante under the Golden Stool. The empire lasts two centuries.

image.title: Ghana, asante, peso per oro a forma di elefante, 1890-1910 ca., da regione di ashanti.JPG

h-panipat-1526.summary: Babur defeats the Sultan of Delhi at Panipat. His Mughal dynasty comes to rule most of India.

image.title: The battle of Panipat and the death of Sultan Ibrāhīm, the last of the Lōdī Sultans of Delhi.jpg
image.artist: Ẓahīr ud-Dīn Muḥammad Bābur (1483-1530) It contains 30 mostly full-page miniatures in fine Mughal style by at least two different artists.

h-taj-mahal.summary: Shah Jahan builds a white marble tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

h-plassey.summary: The British East India Company defeats the Nawab of Bengal. British rule in India begins to grow.

image.title: Lord Clive meeting with Mir Jafar after the Battle of Plassey.jpg

h-macau.summary: Portuguese traders found a settlement on the south China coast. It stays Portuguese until 1999.

h-imjin-war.summary: Japanese armies invade Korea twice. Korea and Ming China drive them out.

h-sekigahara.summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins control of Japan in a great battle.

image.title: Sekigaharascreen.jpg
image.artist: User LordAmeth on en.wikipedia Collection of The Town of Sekigahara Archive of History and Cultural Anthropology

h-tokugawa-shogunate.summary: The Tokugawa shoguns rule Japan from Edo for more than two and a half centuries.

h-qing-beijing.summary: The Manchu Qing dynasty takes the Ming capital. It rules China until 1912.

image.title: Flag of China (1889–1912).svg
image.artist: Original: zh:清朝政府 Vector: Sodacan

h-malacca-1511.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque takes the great trading port on the Strait of Malacca.

image.title: Conquista de Malaca, estudo - Ernesto Condeixa (cropped).png

h-manila-1571.summary: Miguel López de Legazpi makes Manila the capital of the Spanish Philippines. Its galleons link Asia and the Americas.

h-batavia.summary: The Dutch East India Company builds its Asian headquarters on Java.

image.title: Collectie NMvWereldculturen, TM-60036462, Foto, 'De Kali Besar Zuid in de Chinese wijk van Batavia', fotograaf onbekend, 1925-1938.jpg
image.artist: Photo: View this image on the website of the Nationaal Museum van Wereldculturen

h-dzungars.summary: Western Mongol peoples unite in Dzungaria. They later build the Dzungar Khanate.

h-fall-of-tenochtitlan.summary: Hernán Cortés and his Indigenous allies take the Aztec capital. Spanish rule of Mexico begins.

h-cajamarca.summary: Spanish soldiers seize the last Sapa Inca at Cajamarca. The conquest of the Inca Empire begins.

image.title: La Captura de Atahualpa - Juan Lepiani 1920s.png

h-potosi.summary: Silver from a mountain in the Andes makes Potosí rich. It becomes a major city of the Spanish Empire.

image.title: Vista de la Villa Imperial de Potosí.jpg

h-jamestown.summary: The Virginia Company founds the first lasting English settlement in North America.

h-plymouth-colony.summary: English separatists from the Mayflower found the first permanent colony in New England.

h-declaration-of-independence.summary: Thirteen American colonies declare independence from Great Britain.

image.title: United States Declaration of Independence.jpg
image.artist: original: w:Second Continental Congress ; reproduction: William Stone

h-us-constitution.summary: Delegates in Philadelphia draft a new framework of government for the United States.

image.title: Constitution of the United States - DPLA - 9ca804144bd5965e992ae3528bc3c6a3 (page 1).jpg

h-haitian-revolution.summary: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rise against French rule. They found the free nation of Haiti.

image.title: Incendie de la Plaine du Cap. Massacre des Blancs par les esclaves noirs révoltés. France militaire. Martinet et Masson.jpg

h-tasman-1642.summary: A Dutch voyage reaches Tasmania and New Zealand. It is the first known European visit to either.

image.title: Abel Tasman Navigateur en Australie (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Photo: State Library of New South Wales

h-cook-first-voyage.summary: Cook observes the transit of Venus at Tahiti. He then charts New Zealand and the east coast of Australia.

image.title: HMS Endeavour off the coast of New Holland, by Samuel Atkins c.1794.jpg

h-first-fleet.summary: British ships carrying convicts found a penal colony at Port Jackson. Colonization of Australia begins.

image.title: A view of Botany Bay A1475003h (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Original drawing by R. Cleveley, engraving by T. Medland.

h-slave-trade-act-1807.summary: Parliament prohibits the Atlantic slave trade across the British Empire.

image.title: Coat of Arms of the United Kingdom (1801-1816).svg

h-waterloo.summary: A coalition army defeats Napoleon in Belgium. His rule of France ends.

h-origin-of-species.summary: Charles Darwin sets out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

h-german-empire.summary: The German states unite under Prussia. The new empire is proclaimed at Versailles.

image.title: A v Werner - Kaiserproklamation am 18 Januar 1871 (3. Fassung 1885).jpg

h-world-war-i.summary: An assassination in Sarajevo sets off a global war between two great alliances. Millions die.

h-russian-revolution.summary: Revolution ends the Russian monarchy. The Bolsheviks seize power later that year.

image.title: Митинг на Невском проспекте (1917).jpg
image.artist: Photo: Museum of Political History of Russia

h-world-war-ii.summary: Germany's invasion of Poland begins a world war between the Allies and the Axis. It is the deadliest war in history.

h-world-wide-web.summary: Tim Berners-Lee invents the Web at CERN. It opens to the public in 1993.

h-berlin-wall.summary: East Germany opens the border in Berlin. The division of Europe begins to end.

image.title: West and East Germans at the Brandenburg Gate in 1989.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Original photo by unknown author. Reproduction from public documentation/memorial by Lear 21 at English Wikipedia .

h-soviet-dissolution.summary: The Soviet Union ceases to exist. Fifteen republics become independent states.

h-ottoman-sultanate-abolished.summary: Turkey's Grand National Assembly abolishes the sultanate. The Republic of Turkey follows.

h-israel-1948.summary: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel. War with neighboring Arab states follows.

h-iranian-revolution.summary: A revolution overthrows the Pahlavi monarchy. Iran becomes an Islamic republic.

image.title: Mass demonstration in Iran, date unknown.jpg

h-sokoto-caliphate.summary: Usman dan Fodio founds a caliphate in what is now northern Nigeria. It becomes West Africa's most populous state.

h-liberia-1847.summary: Settlers in a colony founded for freed Black Americans declare Liberia independent.

h-suez-canal.summary: A canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Ships no longer need to sail around Africa.

h-adwa.summary: Emperor Menelik II's army defeats an Italian invasion. Ethiopia keeps its independence.

h-year-of-africa.summary: Seventeen African nations win independence in a single year. Nigeria is the most populous of them.

image.title: Patrice Lumumba signs the document granting independence to the Congo next to Belgian Prime Minister Gaston Eyskens.jpg

h-south-africa-1994.summary: Citizens of all races vote for the first time. Apartheid ends, and Nelson Mandela becomes president.

h-rwandan-genocide.summary: Extremists carry out a genocide against the Tutsi during Rwanda's civil war.

h-indian-rebellion-1857.summary: Soldiers and civilians rise against the East India Company. Britain then takes direct rule of India.

image.title: Felice Beato (British, born Italy - (Exterior of The Secundra Bagh) - Google Art Project.jpg

h-partition-of-india.summary: British rule ends and India and Pakistan become independent. Partition uproots millions of people.

image.title: A refugee special train at Ambala Station during partition of India.jpg

h-bangladesh-1971.summary: After a war of liberation, East Pakistan becomes the independent nation of Bangladesh.

h-first-opium-war.summary: Britain goes to war with Qing China over the opium trade. China cedes Hong Kong.

image.title: Destroying Chinese war junks, by E. Duncan (1843).jpg

h-meiji-restoration.summary: Power returns to Japan's emperor. Japan modernizes rapidly.

h-xinhai-revolution.summary: An uprising at Wuchang brings down the Qing dynasty. China becomes a republic.

h-hiroshima-nagasaki.summary: The United States drops two atomic bombs on Japanese cities. Japan surrenders weeks later.

h-prc-1949.summary: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic in Tiananmen Square.

h-korean-war.summary: North and South Korea fight a war that draws in the United Nations and China. It ends in an armistice.

image.title: Chosin.jpg
image.artist: Photo by Corporal Peter McDonald, USMC

h-covid-19.summary: A new coronavirus spreads from Wuhan across the world in early 2020. The WHO ends the global emergency in May 2023.

image.title: Covid-19 SP - UTI V. Nova Cachoeirinha.jpg

h-indonesia-1945.summary: Sukarno reads the proclamation of independence. A war against Dutch rule follows.

h-fall-of-saigon.summary: North Vietnam captures Saigon. The Vietnam War ends.

image.title: The air evacuation of siege-stricken Vietnamese from Saigon to the U.S. was conducted after the Babylift operation.... - NARA - 542335.tif
image.artist: Photo: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration

h-indian-ocean-tsunami.summary: A huge earthquake off Sumatra sends tsunamis across the Indian Ocean.

image.title: US Navy 050102-N-9593M-040 A village near the coast of Sumatra lays in ruin after the Tsunami that struck South East Asia.jpg
image.artist: U.S. Navy photo by Photographer's Mate 2nd Class Philip A. McDaniel

h-tashkent-1865.summary: Russian forces attack Tashkent during their conquest of Central Asia.

h-sputnik.summary: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial satellite. The space age begins.

image.title: Первый в мире искусственный спутник Земли.jpg

h-louisiana-purchase.summary: The United States buys the vast Louisiana territory from France.

image.title: Louisiana Purchase New Orleans Thure de Thulstrup.jpg

h-mexican-independence.summary: A long struggle ends Spanish rule in Mexico.

h-ayacucho.summary: Patriot forces defeat the last large Spanish army in South America.

image.title: Batalla de Ayacucho by Martín Tovar y Tovar (1827 - 1902).jpg

h-american-civil-war.summary: The Union and the Confederacy fight over slavery and secession. The Union wins, and slavery ends.

image.title: Battle of Gettysburg, by Currier and Ives.png
image.artist: Nathaniel Currier and James Merritt Ives

h-transcontinental-railroad.summary: A golden spike joins the rails across the United States at Promontory Summit.

image.title: East and West Shaking hands at the laying of last rail Union Pacific Railroad - Restoration.jpg

h-lei-aurea.summary: Princess Isabel signs the Golden Law, ending slavery in Brazil.

h-panama-canal.summary: A canal across Panama links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

image.title: Opening of the Panama Canal SS Ancon approaching Gamboa Looking north Aug 15, 1914 - DPLA - 0c0baedc6b427a89406d5779c16b4205.jpg

h-wall-street-crash.summary: Stock prices collapse in New York. The worldwide Great Depression follows.

h-united-nations.summary: Delegates from around the world sign the charter that founds the United Nations.

h-apollo-11.summary: American astronauts become the first people to walk on the Moon.

image.title: A Man on the Moon, AS11-40-5903 (cropped).jpg

h-september-11.summary: Al-Qaeda hijackers crash airliners in New York and near Washington. Nearly 3,000 people die.

h-treaty-of-waitangi.summary: The British Crown and Māori chiefs sign a treaty. New Zealand becomes a British colony.

image.title: Treatyofwaitangi.jpg
image.artist: William Hobson, James Freeman, and James Busby (English version); Henry Williams and Edward Williams (Māori translation)

h-nz-womens-suffrage.summary: A new law gives New Zealand women the vote. They vote in a general election that November.

image.title: Tribute to the Suffragettes, Christchurch, NZ - cropped.jpg

h-australia-federation.summary: Six British colonies unite as the Commonwealth of Australia.

image.title: Town Hall, Sydney, Inauguration of Australian Commonwealth.jpg

h-ur-iii-falls.summary: Elamite invaders sack Ur and end its last great dynasty. Genesis names Ur as Abram's first home.

image.title: Ziggarut of Ur - M.Lubinski.jpg
image.artist: Michael Lubinski from Green Bay, WI, USA

h-middle-kingdom-egypt.summary: Egypt is reunited under Theban kings. Trade and literature flourish along the Nile.

image.title: Statues of Senusret III, British Museum 01.jpg

h-mari-archives.summary: Thousands of clay letters survive from Mari on the Euphrates. They show the tribal world of the patriarchs' era.

h-hittite-kingdom.summary: The Hittites rule central Anatolia from Hattusa. The Bible names Hittites among the peoples of Canaan.

h-hatshepsut.summary: A queen takes the full title of pharaoh. Her temple at Deir el-Bahari still stands.

image.title: Seated Statue of Hatshepsut MET Hatshepsut2012 (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Photo: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art . See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

h-battle-of-megiddo-1457.summary: Egypt defeats a league of Canaanite kings. Canaan stays under Egyptian rule for centuries.

h-amarna-letters.summary: Canaanite kings write to the pharaoh for help. Several complain of raiders called the Habiru.

image.title: Five Amarna letters on display at the British Museum, LondonA.jpg

h-ramesses-ii.summary: Egypt's most famous builder reigns for 66 years. Many link the Exodus story to his era.

h-merneptah-stele.summary: A pharaoh's victory hymn lists Israel among the peoples of Canaan. It is the oldest known mention of Israel outside the Bible.

h-ugarit-destroyed.summary: The Canaanite port city burns and is never rebuilt. Its tablets show the worship of Baal and El.

h-sea-peoples.summary: Egypt drives back seafaring raiders. One group, the Peleset, settles the coast as the Philistines.

image.title: Medinet Habu Ramses III. Tempel Nordostwand Abzeichnung 01.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Gray, Dorothea (1974) "chapter G" in (in German) Seewesen , Archaeologia Homerica, I, Göttingen , pp. 166−167

h-philistine-pentapolis.summary: The Philistines build five cities on Canaan's coast. They are Israel's rivals in Judges and Samuel.

h-phoenician-alphabet.summary: A short alphabet of 22 letters spreads from the Levant coast. Hebrew, Greek, and Latin letters descend from it.

h-khirbet-qeiyafa.summary: A walled town guards the Valley of Elah. It dates to the time of Saul and David.

h-hiram-of-tyre.summary: The Phoenician king of Tyre trades cedar and craftsmen. The Bible makes him an ally of David and Solomon.

h-gezer-calendar.summary: A small limestone tablet lists the farming months. It is one of the oldest Hebrew inscriptions.

h-shoshenq-campaign.summary: The pharaoh lists the towns he conquered on a wall at Karnak. Many link him to Shishak in 1 Kings 14.

h-neo-assyrian-empire.summary: Assyria builds the largest empire yet seen. Its kings will conquer Israel and besiege Jerusalem.

image.title: Lamassu from the North-West Palace at Nimrud, Iraq, 9th century BC. The British Museum.jpg

h-battle-of-qarqar.summary: A league of kings meets Shalmaneser III in Syria. Assyrian records say Ahab brought 2,000 chariots.

h-mesha-stele.summary: Mesha boasts of throwing off Israel's rule. 2 Kings 3 tells the same revolt from Israel's side.

image.title: P1120870 Louvre stèle de Mésha AO5066 rwk.JPG

h-tel-dan-stele.summary: An Aramean king boasts of killing two kings. One belonged to the house of David.

h-black-obelisk.summary: Shalmaneser III records the tribute of Jehu of Israel. It is the only known picture of a king of Israel.

image.title: The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III, 9th century BC, from Nimrud, Iraq. The British Museum.jpg

h-tiglath-pileser-iii.summary: The king called Pul in the Bible takes tribute from Israel. He deports whole peoples to hold his empire.

h-sargon-ii.summary: Sargon claims to have carried off 27,290 people of Samaria. He builds a new capital at Khorsabad.

image.title: Sargon II, Iraq Museum in Baghdad.jpg

h-taharqa.summary: A Kushite pharaoh rules from the Nile to the Delta. 2 Kings 19 names him Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia.

h-siloam-inscription.summary: Diggers cut a tunnel through rock to bring spring water inside Jerusalem. An inscription tells how the two crews met.

h-sennacherib-annals.summary: Clay prisms record the campaign of 701 BCE. They say Hezekiah was shut up in Jerusalem like a caged bird.

image.title: Taylor Prism-3.jpg
