h-lachish-reliefs.summary: Assyria storms Judah's second city. Sennacherib's palace walls show the siege in carved stone.

h-esarhaddon.summary: Sennacherib's son takes Memphis from Taharqa. Assyria reaches its greatest extent.

image.title: Detail. Sam'al stele of Esarhaddon, 671 BCE, Pergamon Museum.jpg

h-psamtik-i.summary: A king from Sais reunites Egypt. His dynasty fights Babylon in Jeremiah's day.

image.title: Bust from Statue of a King MET EGX.358.jpeg
image.artist: Photo: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art . See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

h-lydian-coins.summary: The kingdom of Lydia stamps lumps of electrum with a mark of value. Coinage spreads across the Greek world.

h-ketef-hinnom.summary: Two tiny silver amulets carry the priestly blessing of Numbers 6. They are the oldest known Bible text.

image.title: Kettef Hinnom scrolls1.jpg
image.artist: Photo: Edited version of an image of the Kettef Hinnom scrolls

h-battle-of-megiddo-609.summary: Pharaoh Necho II marches north to help Assyria. King Josiah of Judah tries to stop him and is killed.

h-battle-of-carchemish-605.summary: Nebuchadnezzar routs Necho's army on the Euphrates. Judah passes from Egypt's sway to Babylon's.

h-nebuchadnezzar-ii.summary: Babylon's greatest king takes Jerusalem twice and rebuilds his capital in glazed brick.

h-babylonian-chronicle-597.summary: A clay tablet says Nebuchadnezzar seized the city of Judah and appointed a new king. 2 Kings 24 tells the same events.

image.title: ABC 05 Early Years of Nebuchadnezzar chronicle.jpg

h-jehoiachin-ration-tablets.summary: Palace ration lists name Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and his sons. 2 Kings 25 ends with his release.

h-apries.summary: Apries sends an army to relieve besieged Jerusalem but fails. Jeremiah 44 names him Pharaoh Hophra.

h-lachish-letters.summary: Officers at Lachish write on potsherds as Babylon closes in. Jeremiah 34 names Lachish among the last cities standing.

image.title: Steen met inscriptie in het Lahish schrift, Bestanddeelnr 255-6141.jpg

h-ishtar-gate.summary: Nebuchadnezzar builds a blue glazed gate with dragons and bulls. Judah's exiles would have known it.

h-nabonidus.summary: Babylon's last king spends years at an Arabian oasis. His son Belshazzar governs, as in Daniel 5.

image.title: Detail, stele of Nabonidus. Nabonidus wears the traditional dress of a Babylonian king, holding objects symbolizing justice and power.jpg

h-fall-of-babylon.summary: Persian forces enter Babylon and end its empire. The Jewish exiles soon receive leave to go home.

image.title: The fall of Babylon; Cyrus the Great defeating the Chaldean Wellcome V0034440.jpg
image.artist: Photo: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/fc/fc/32d4c8b927dea8bfbf69f55cbd10.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/V0034440.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-03): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/pc9e75j3 CC-BY-4.0

h-cyrus-cylinder.summary: Cyrus records that he let deported peoples return home with their gods. Ezra 1 gives his decree for the Jews.

h-kingdom-of-saba.summary: Sabaeans grow rich on the incense trade from southern Arabia. Many link them to the Queen of Sheba.

h-darius-the-great.summary: Darius reorganizes the Persian Empire into provinces. Ezra 6 says he let the temple in Jerusalem be finished.

h-behistun-inscription.summary: Darius carves his story on a cliff in three languages. It later became the key to reading cuneiform.

h-xerxes-i.summary: Xerxes rules Persia from Susa and Persepolis. Many identify him with King Ahasuerus in the book of Esther.

h-battle-of-salamis.summary: The Athenian fleet wrecks the Persian navy in a narrow strait. Xerxes retreats to Asia.

image.title: Kaulbach, Wilhelm von - Die Seeschlacht bei Salamis - 1868.JPG

h-artaxerxes-i.summary: The Persian king of Ezra 7 and Nehemiah 2 rules for forty years. He faces a long revolt in Egypt.

image.title: Relief of Artaxerxes I, from his tomb in Naqsh-e Rustam.jpg

h-herodotus.summary: A Greek traveler writes the first great history of the Persian Wars. He describes Babylon, Egypt, and Persia.

image.title: Marble bust of Herodotos MET DT11742 (cropped).jpg
image.artist: Photo: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the Metropolitan Museum of Art . See the Image and Data Resources Open Access Policy

h-elephantine-papyri.summary: Jewish soldiers guard Egypt's southern border for Persia. Their letters name Sanballat and the high priest Johanan.

image.title: Papyrus narrating the story of the wise chancellor Ahiqar. Aramaic script. 5th century BCE. From Elephantine, Egypt. Neues Museum.jpg

h-trial-of-socrates.summary: The philosopher is condemned for impiety and corrupting the youth. He drinks hemlock.

image.title: Socrates Address by Belgian artist Louis Joseph Lebrun, 1867.jpg

h-siege-of-tyre-332.summary: Alexander builds a causeway to the island city and takes it after seven months. Ezekiel 26 foretold Tyre's ruin.

image.title: A naval action during the siege of Tyre by Andre Castaigne (1898-1899).jpg

h-alexandria-founded.summary: A new Greek city rises on Egypt's coast. It becomes home to the largest Jewish community outside Judea.

h-ptolemaic-kingdom.summary: Alexander's general Ptolemy founds a Greek dynasty in Egypt. Judea lies under its rule for a century.

image.title: Gold coin of Ptolemy I Soter.jpg

h-septuagint.summary: Jews in Alexandria translate the books of Moses into Greek. The Septuagint becomes the Bible of the early Church.

image.title: Codex Vaticanus (1 Esdras 1-55 to 2-5) (The S.S. Teacher's Edition-The Holy Bible).jpg
image.artist: Photo: Codex Vaticanus (Gregory-Aland no. B or 03)

h-antiochus-iv.summary: The Seleucid king bans the Sabbath and circumcision. He sets up a pagan altar in the temple.

h-maccabean-revolt.summary: Judas Maccabeus leads a revolt against Seleucid rule. The temple is cleansed in 164 BCE, the origin of Hanukkah.

image.title: Bronze prutah of John Hyrcanus I.jpg

h-hasmonean-dynasty.summary: The Maccabees' family rules Judea as priests and kings. Herod ends the line with Roman help.

h-dead-sea-scrolls.summary: Scribes copy and hide hundreds of scrolls near the Dead Sea. They hold the oldest known copies of most Old Testament books.

h-pompey-takes-jerusalem.summary: A Roman general settles a Hasmonean civil war by force. Judea becomes a Roman client state.

image.title: Pompée dans le Temple de Jérusalem.jpg

h-herod-the-great.summary: Rome's client king takes Jerusalem and rules with an iron hand. Matthew 2 sets the birth of Jesus in his last years.

image.title: HerodtheGreat2.jpg

h-caesarea-maritima.summary: Herod builds a great artificial harbor on an open coast. Caesarea becomes Rome's seat in Judea and Paul's prison.

image.title: Caesarea.JPG
image.artist: The original uploader was אסף.צ at Hebrew Wikipedia .

h-herods-temple.summary: Herod enlarges the temple and its courts on a vast new platform. This is the temple Jesus taught in.

h-herod-archelaus.summary: Herod's son rules Judea until Rome deposes him. Matthew 2 says Joseph feared him and settled in Nazareth.

h-census-of-quirinius.summary: Rome counts Judea's people and property for taxes. Luke 2 links a census under Quirinius to Jesus's birth.

image.title: Meister der Kahriye-Cami-Kirche in Istanbul 005.jpg
image.artist: Master of the Church of the Holy Saviour in Chora, Istanbul

h-tiberius.summary: Augustus's stepson rules the empire. Luke 3 dates John the Baptist's preaching to his fifteenth year.

image.title: 8095 - Roma - Ara Pacis - Tiberio - Foto Giovanni Dall'Orto - 28-Mar-2008.jpg

h-caiaphas.summary: Rome's prefect appoints Caiaphas high priest. He presides when Jesus is brought before the council.

image.title: Gerard van Honthorst - Christ before the High Priest - WGA11650 (cropped).jpg

h-herod-antipas.summary: Herod's son rules Galilee during Jesus's ministry. He beheads John the Baptist. Caligula exiles him in 39.

h-pontius-pilate.summary: The Roman prefect governs from Caesarea for ten years. A stone found there in 1961 bears his name.

h-philo-embassy.summary: The Jewish philosopher leads an embassy after riots in Alexandria. His writings shaped early Christian thought.

h-herod-agrippa-i.summary: Claudius gives Herod's grandson all of Judea. Acts 12 says he killed James and died suddenly at Caesarea.

h-delphi-inscription.summary: A letter of Claudius names Gallio as governor of Achaia. It helps date Paul's stay in Corinth in Acts 18.

h-antonius-felix.summary: The Roman procurator holds Paul at Caesarea for two years, as Acts 24 tells.

h-porcius-festus.summary: The new procurator hears Paul with King Agrippa II. Paul appeals to Caesar and sails for Rome.

image.title: Coin of Porcius Festus.jpg
image.artist: Original uploader was Atzmonit at Hebrew Wikipedia . The pictures of coins are Itamar . Later version(s) were uploaded by Alorkezas at en.wikipedia

h-nero.summary: The last emperor of Augustus's line rules Rome. Christian tradition says Peter and Paul died under him.

h-great-fire-of-rome.summary: Fire destroys much of the city. Nero blames the Christians and has many put to death.

h-first-jewish-roman-war.summary: Riots in Caesarea grow into a full revolt. Rome answers with an army that will destroy Jerusalem.

image.title: Arch of Titus Menorah.png
image.artist: derivative work: Steerpike ( talk ) Arc_de_Triumph_copy.jpg : user: בית השלום

h-siege-of-masada.summary: Romans build a great ramp to the desert fortress. Josephus says the defenders died rather than surrender.

h-arch-of-titus.summary: A triumphal arch in Rome shows soldiers carrying the temple's menorah from Jerusalem.

image.title: Arch Titus, Forum Romanum, Rome, Italy.jpg

h-domitian.summary: Many scholars date John's exile on Patmos and the book of Revelation to his reign.

image.title: Domiziano da collezione albani, fine del I sec. dc. 02.JPG

h-josephus-antiquities.summary: A Jewish historian in Rome retells Israel's story for Greek readers. He mentions John the Baptist and James.

image.title: Joseph, son of Gorian, called Flavius Josephus (cropped).jpg

h-bar-kokhba-revolt.summary: A last Jewish revolt is crushed by Hadrian. Jews are barred from Jerusalem, renamed Aelia Capitolina.

h-izapa.summary: A ceremonial center near the Pacific coast of Chiapas carves narrative stelae. Its style links the Olmec and the Maya.

h-kaminaljuyu.summary: A great highland city builds canals and mounds in the Valley of Guatemala. It trades widely across the region.

h-takalik-abaj.summary: A trading city on Guatemala's Pacific slope raises carved monuments. Olmec and Maya styles meet there.

image.title: ESTRUCTURA 12 MUSEO AL AIRE LIBRE FACHADA OESTE - TAKALIK ABAJ.png

h-san-bartolo-murals.summary: Painters cover a temple room with a Maya creation story and an early king. Some of the oldest Maya writing is found here.

image.title: SBmural.jpg
image.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Authenticmaya~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).

h-nazca-lines.summary: People on Peru's desert coast scrape huge lines and figures into the ground. Many can be seen whole only from the air.

image.title: Líneas de Nazca, Nazca, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 49.JPG

h-chiapa-de-corzo-stela-2.summary: A carved panel in Chiapas records a date in the Mesoamerican Long Count calendar. No earlier example is known.

h-tres-zapotes-stela-c.summary: A Gulf Coast monument bears a Long Count date and Epi-Olmec writing. It shows Olmec traditions living on.

h-hopewell.summary: Peoples of the Ohio valley build great earthworks. They trade copper, shell, and mica across the continent.

h-la-mojarra-stela.summary: A Veracruz monument carries a long text in Epi-Olmec script. It shows a ruler in elaborate dress.

h-pyramid-of-the-sun.summary: Builders raise one of the largest pyramids in the Americas. Teotihuacan becomes the great power of central Mexico.

image.title: 2020-02-11 Teotihuacan la Avenida de los Muertos y la Pirámide del Sol.jpg

h-xitle-cuicuilco.summary: Lava covers a city in the Valley of Mexico. Its people scatter, and Teotihuacan grows stronger.

image.title: Western side of the circular pyramid at Cuicuilco. (32961693441).jpg

h-siyaj-kak.summary: Siyaj K'ak' arrives at Tikal, and its king dies the same day. New rulers tied to Teotihuacan take power.
